{{Quote|If the wind no longer calls to you, it is time to see if you have forgotten your name.|[[Elegos A'Kla]]|<ref name="I, Jedi">''[[I, Jedi]]''</ref>}}
The '''Caamasi''' {{Pronounced|kɑɑ'mɑsi}} were a [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Mammal/Legends|mammalian]] species of furred [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoids]] known for their compassionate and peace-loving nature; indeed, the name ''Caamasi'' came to mean "friend from afar" and "stranger to be trusted" in some languages across [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]].

==Biology and appearance==
[[File:Caamasi-KOTOR46.jpg|thumb|left|180px|A Caamasi baring claws and fangs]]
A [[Species/Legends|species]] of furry [[Mammal/Legends|mammalians]], the Caamasi were covered in dense grey or brown fur and had a spicy, woody body scent that was similar to that of [[Corellian whiskey/Legends|Corellian whiskey]]. They had two, long arms with thin, three-fingered hands,<ref name="TFUCG" /> and two pointed ears which stuck out from the sides of their heads.<ref name="NEGAS" /> They also had extremely acute senses of smell, with their nose positioned at the end of a tooth-filled snout.

Caamasi had the interesting ability to share vivid memories called [[Memnis|''memnii'']] with their near relatives and [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitives]], especially members of the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]]. A ''memnis'' was as vivid to one who received it as it was to the one who participated in the event remembered. Their peace-loving natures were accounted for in part due to ''memnii'', as having a memory of killing or harming would be particularly strong, becoming unbearable in time, and something Caamasi would seek to avoid except in defense of themselves or others, for which case they would accept their burden.<ref name="UAA" />

==Society and culture==
[[File:Caamasi-TFUCG.png|thumb|right|160px|A Caamasi]]
A pacifist race, culture on Caamasi evolved around the basic tenets of peace and social justice; influencing the evolution of the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] and their service as [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Knights]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. Working as explorers, diplomats, and artists, the Caamasi were a monogamous people who valued single partners while mating and starting a family. So culturally ingrained was this notion that there was great debate among the species following the devastation of their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]]. The Caamasi who were off-world at the time considered evolving to a position of polygamy so as to regrow the population. While the argument was one of survival, many sociologists familiar with the culture of the Caamasi believed that they would not accept the idea.<ref name="NEGAS" /> The famed celebration known as the [[Rainbow of Sunshine Festival]] was held on Caamas annually and beloved by the populace.<ref name="Republic HoloNet News Special Inaugural Edition 16:5:241">{{InsiderCite|84|Republic HoloNet News Special Inaugural Edition 16:5:241}}</ref>

==History==
{{Quote|They were an almost universally beloved people.|[[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa Solo]] to [[Talon Karrde]]|<ref name="Specter of the Past">''[[Specter of the Past]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Political_Strategist_DA.png|thumb|left|250px|A Caamasi political strategist]]
Caamasi possessed great moral strength and respect for others. They were among the galaxy's finest diplomats and mediators, often solving severe conflicts in a matter of days. Indeed, as the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] began to evolve on [[Ossus/Legends|Ossus]], [[Lore Keeper|Jedi scholars]] studied on Caamas and drew upon the teachings of [[Hespecia Tik'kla]] when creating the [[Jedi Code/Legends|Jedi Code]].<ref name="TJP">[[The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force (real-life book)|''The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force'']]</ref> Many millennia later, [[Arden Lyn]] would cite Caamasi influence on the Jedi Order as being a factor in the [[First Great Schism|schism]] between the Order and the [[Legions of Lettow]].<ref name="Warfare">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref>

During the last stages of the [[Pius Dea Crusades]] around [[11,000 BBY]], the Caamasi opposed the [[Pius Dea]]-controlled [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic's]] [[inquisition]]s against domestic opposition. They succeeded in persuading the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] to end their centuries-long [[Recusal]] and collaborated with the Jedi and [[Alsakan/Legends|Alsakani]] to mastermind an anti-Pius Dea heresy which developed into the [[Renunciates]] movement by [[10,967 BBY]]. During the [[Seventh Alsakan Conflict]], the Caamasi were part of a broad anti-Pius Dea coalition which toppled the sect and ended its grip on the Republic. Following the [[Battle of Uquine]], the last Pius Dea [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Contispex XIX]] was tried and imprisoned for life on Caamas.<ref name="Warfare" />

During the last days of the Galactic Republic, Senior Anthropologist [[Mammon Hoole]] witnessed the Caamasi prowess firsthand when they negotiated peace between the [[Kubaz/Legends|Kubaz]] and the [[Verpine/Legends|Verpine]]. Unfortunately, the Caamasi pacifism was at odds with [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine's]] [[New Order/Legends|New Order]], and they suffered greatly under [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] rule. A few months after the end of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the surface of their homeworld, [[Caamas/Legends|Caamas]], was [[Caamas Firestorm|bombarded]], killing millions. After the destruction of their planet's environment, many refugees moved to [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]], [[Kerilt]], and [[Susevfi]]. The bombardment was aided by a group of [[Bothan/Legends|Bothans]] who sabotaged Caamas' [[Deflector shield generator/Legends|shield generators]]. The [[Caamas Document]] detailed their involvement. Although many demanded that the Bothans purchase an uninhabited planet and terraform it according to Caamas' specifications, the Caamasi chose to forgive those guilty of harming them.<ref name="NEGAS" />

Following years of struggling to repopulate the species, the [[Caamasi Remnant]] and its leader, [[Elegos A'Kla]], joined the [[New Republic Senate/Legends|New Republic Senate]] and participated in the hazardous political turmoil surrounding the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]].<ref name="NEGAS" />

==Caamasi in the galaxy==
[[File:Caamasi_FI.jpg|thumb|200px|[[Eg'ros Akala]] is arrested on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]].]]
The Caamasi who found themselves away from their homeworld typically worked as diplomats or law-givers at the side of politicians and planetary rulers across the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. The most famed Caamasi of the [[New Republic era]] was [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Elegos A'Kla]], a representative of the [[Caamasi Remnant]]. His place in the Senate was filled by his daughter, [[Releqy A'Kla]], following his execution at the hands of the [[Yuuzhan Vong]].<ref name="NEGAS" /> [[Ves Volette]] was a famed Caamasari [[light sculptor]] whose murder was investigated by Jedi turned [[Private investigator/Legends|private investigator]] [[Jax Pavan]] in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]].<ref name="Coruscant Nights II: Street of Shadows">''[[Coruscant Nights II: Street of Shadows]]''</ref> 

[[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitives]] in Caamasi society were celebrated and while few went on to join the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]], those who did often found themselves training in the ways of the [[Jedi Consular]]. [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Ylenic It'kla]] served with distinction during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] and exiled himself to [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]] during the [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|Great Jedi Purge]], serving as an advisor to [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Bail Prestor Organa/Legends|Bail Organa]] until his death.<ref name="EI">{{InsiderCite|66|Elusion Illusion}}</ref>
